messages:
Jordan (AcmeApp): Hey @support — we started seeing persistent 429s in prod ~2026-03-17T08:12 PST. Affected users show repeated failures when the app refreshes. Example request ids: req_01a2b3c4, req_01a2b3c5, req_01a2b3c6. We're on the hosted API (org_id: org-acme-77). App polls every 15s with no jitter; many customers opened the app at 08:11 and traffic spiked. Sample response:

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
content-type: application/json
{
  "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
  "message": "organization rate limit exceeded",
  "request_id": "req_01a2b3c4"
}

I can reproduce with curl if you want. Not seeing auth errors, just 429s. Any quick triage steps?

Mia (Support): Sorry about that — we'll dig in. Can you confirm the exact org_id (thanks, got org-acme-77) and paste a raw curl you used (with auth redacted)? Also are these users all in the same region/locale? We'll check rate-limiter logs and escalate to SRE if needed.

Jordan (AcmeApp): Curl we used (token replaced with X):

curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer X" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"input":"ping"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

All affected clients are in NA-west region. We confirmed average per-device request rate ~4 req/min (poll every 15s). No retries in client (we pushed aggressive retry code earlier without jitter).

Sam (SRE): I pulled the rate-limiter metrics for org-acme-77 — they're hitting the org-level RPM bucket and an internal per-tenant TPM protection. Looks like a classic synchronized-polling thundering-herd: many clients align to minute boundaries. Two quick checks: (1) can you paste a few full request IDs from an affected session so I can search the edge logs? (2) can you run a single-step repro with this header to get deterministic logs: `-H "X-Debug-Request: repro-<your-id>"`?

Jordan (AcmeApp): Here are full request ids from a single incident window: req_01a2b3c4 req_01a2b3c5 req_01a2b3c6. Ran repro with debug header — got immediate 429 with request_id repro-01a2b3c7. Response includes `x-rate-limit-reset: 22` header.

Alina (Eng): Thanks — a couple notes from runtime side: (a) We see minute-bucket collisions across AZs when lots of clients poll at aligned intervals. The rate-limiter uses fixed 60s windows by default which makes spikes worse if many clients hit near boundary. (b) If clients open many short TCP connections instead of reusing HTTP/2 streams, we also observe per-connection token overheads. Short-term fixes: add jitter/exponential backoff clientside; use HTTP/2 multiplexing or keepalive; or switch to streaming/push for frequent updates.

Mia (Support): Operationally we can do two things: (1) request a temporary quota uplift for org-acme-77 while they deploy a client patch, (2) enable a targeted 24h relax rule that gives a higher burst window to avoid immediate 429s. Jordan — want us to open the uplift now? Also please schedule client patch ETA.

Jordan (AcmeApp): Yes please for the 24h relax. We'll ship a client patch tonight that adds randomized jitter to polls and exponential backoff on 429s. ETA ~23:00 PST. If you can relax limits until then that would be huge.

Sam (SRE): Filed internal incident INC-2026-543 and requested a 2x temporary org RPM uplift for 24h. Monitoring alert created for abnormal sync patterns (threshold: >50 identical timestamps / 60s). I also added a debug sampling bucket to capture raw headers for repro-01a2b3c7. I'll post the ticket link once it's live.

ratebot: Rule change applied (audit id: audit-98765). Temporary org throttle adjustment: org-acme-77 RPM +2x for 24 hours; monitoring rule firing for synchronized polls enabled.

Mia (Support): Follow-up checklist we've agreed on:
- Client: add jitter and exponential backoff on 429s (randomize poll interval +-25%).
- Client: prefer keepalive / HTTP/2 or move to a streaming endpoint if polling frequently.
- Server: temporary uplift applied; SRE will watch for secondary effects.
- Product: consider adding a public best-practices doc for high-frequency clients.

Alina (Eng): Small engineering note for future: we should consider moving to a sliding window token bucket or a leakage-based limiter for read patterns like polling; it reduces boundary collisions. I'll open a proposal doc after this incident.

Jordan (AcmeApp): Thanks team — uplift confirmed in our logs, 429s dropped immediately after change. We'll ship patch at 23:00 PST and report back if anything persists. Huge help! :heart:

Mia (Support): Glad it helped — keep us posted. If the 24h window isn't enough or you need a staged rollout, ping and we'll coordinate a more permanent quota change or recommend Dedicated capacity if sustained high throughput is expected.

Sam (SRE): Closing loop — please paste any post-patch request ids if you still see 429s. Otherwise we'll let the temporary rule expire after 24h and review metrics.

Jordan (AcmeApp): Will do. Posting a quick snippet of the client jitter patch we'll deploy:

```js
// poll every ~15s +/- 25%
const base = 15000;
const jitter = Math.floor(Math.random() * base * 0.25);
setTimeout(poll, base - jitter + jitter);
```

Thanks again everyone.
